text_excerpt: CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse 2D-3D Alignment CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse 2D-3D Alignment Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2026 Main Track Poster 📌 Aadith Warrier1, Gnana Prakash Punnavajhala1, Siddharth Tourani2, Muhammad Haris Khan3, Avinash Sharma4, Madhava Krishna1 1IIIT Hyderabad, India 2University of Heidelberg, Germany 3MBZUAI, UAE 4IIT Bombay, India arXiv Code NeurIPS Poster TL;DR Instead of whole scenes or objects, CrossWeave trains on patch-point correspondences, the smallest unit of alignment. As a result, a single model can flexibly encode scene and object level embeddings, and sets the state of the art on both benchmarks of cross-modal scene and instance retrieval. Abstract Cross-modal scene and instance retrieval aims to retrieve a corresponding 3D environment or object given query 2D images, serving as a foundational mechanism for spatial reasoning in robotics and AR/VR. Existing methods achieve this by learning alignment only at the level of whole scenes or objects, which provides no supervision for the fine-grained local structure within them. In this work, we show that supervision on a set of sparse 2D-3D correspondences, without scene- or instance-level contrastive objectives, is sufficient to train a single model for both scene- and instance-level retrieval. Specifically, we propose CrossWeave, a novel framework for cross-modal retrieval that learns sparse patch-point alignment, which alone outperforms existing methods. An optimal transport-based aggregator over the aligned features gives further gains by clustering structurally redundant regions, freeing descriptor capacity for semantically distinct local features. CrossWeave achieves state-of-the-art performance on both scene- and instance-level retrieval on ScanNet and 3RScan with a single model, whereas existing methods require separate models for each task. Our results suggest that whole-scene encoding is unnecessary for cross-modal retrieval and that sparse local correspondence supervision is a more effective and flexible alternative. Method Overview of CrossWeave. Top: training from sparse patch-point pairs. Bottom: the same model used for scene and instance retrieval at inference. CrossWeave learns cross-modal retrieval representations from sparse image patch-3D point correspondences rather than scene- or instance-level labels. Given calibrated RGB-D observations and a reconstructed 3D map, visible patch-point pairs are obtained by projecting 3D points into the image plane, filtering occluded points using rendered depth, quantizing valid pixels into DINOv2 patch tokens, and selecting a compact semantically diverse subset using feature-space farthest point sampling. Frozen encoders extract local patch and point features, which are projected by learnable projection matrices Wpatch and Wpoint into a shared embedding space. A shared SALAD aggregator then maps variable-sized sets of local features into fixed-dimensional descriptors. Training combines a local patch-point Lp2p contrastive loss with an aggregated image-point-cloud contrastive loss Li2pc, preserving fine-grained alignment while organizing local evidence into retrieval-ready descriptors. At inference, the same encoders and projection heads serve both tasks: SALAD descriptors are used for scene retrieval and mean-pooled local features for instance retrieval. Sparse local supervision. Training uses a compact, semantically diverse set of visible patch-point pairs instead of whole scenes, with no scene- or instance-level labels. Two contrastive losses. Lp2p aligns each image patch with its 3D point, and Li2pc aligns the SALAD-aggregated image and point-cloud descriptors. One model, two tasks. The same trained network handles both scene and instance retrieval, using SALAD descriptors for scenes and local features for instances. Results Bold: best, underline: second best. † Trained on additional datasets (ArkitScenes + MultiScan). CrossOver (Updated): CrossOver retrained with the same Utonia 3D backbone as CrossWeave. Cross-Modal Scene Retrieval CrossWeave outperforms all baselines on both datasets at every rank. On ScanNet it reaches 61.54 Top-1 recall, 21.16 points above CrossOver (Updated). Since CrossOver (Updated) uses the same Utonia backbone, this suggests that the gain comes from sparse patch-point supervision rather than a stronger 3D encoder. On 3RScan, Top-1 recall rises from 23.57 to 46.50. Method ScanNet 3RScan Top-1Top-5Top-10 Top-1Top-5Top-10 CrossOver 22.4461.8675.32 19.1158.6077.07 CrossOver† 19.8758.0174.36 17.8351.5973.25 CrossOver (Updated) 40.3890.0696.47 23.5766.8884.71 CrossWeave (Ours) 61.5499.36100.0 46.5085.9992.36 Qualitative comparison of cross-modal scene retrieval on ScanNet. Given a set of query RGB images, each model retrieves the most similar 3D scenes from the database. The ground-truth scene is shown on the left, and retrieved scenes are ordered by similarity from left to right. CrossOver and CrossOver (Updated) fail to retrieve the correct scene within the top five results, while CrossWeave retrieves it at rank 1. The remaining retrieved scenes are also semantically consistent, indicating that CrossWeave learns descriptors that capture both local cross-modal correspondences and global scene context. Retrieval results on a 3RScan kitchen and dining scene. CrossWeave demonstrates superior discriminative ability by retrieving the exact scene at rank 1 from highly localized query images, whereas both baseline models completely fail to place the correct match within their top 5 retrievals. Cross-Modal Instance Retrieval Each query object is retrieved among the objects of its own scene. Top-k is computed within each scene and averaged over scenes; R@k% is the percentage of scenes in which at least k% of the objects are retrieved correctly at Top-1. The same single model gives the best instance retrieval: 78.77 Top-1 on ScanNet and 73.50 on 3RScan. The gap widens at stricter thresholds, with R@75% improving over CrossOver (Updated) by 18.27 points on ScanNet and 14.65 points on 3RScan. The Top-3 retrievals are shown with their similarity scores, and the correct match is outlined in green. Ablation: Training Losses Lp2p alone already gives strong instance retrieval but weak scene retrieval. Adding Li2pc with mean pooling improves scene Top-1, and replacing mean pooling with SALAD improves it further, so both the aggregation objective and the aggregation module matter for scenes. Mean pooling with both losses gives the highest instance Top-1, but its scene Top-1 is 9.3 (ScanNet) and 15.9 (3RScan) points lower; the HYBRID model gives the best trade-off across both tasks. Agg. Additional Experiments Comparison with SceneGraphLoc Following the SceneGraphLoc protocol, each query image is ranked against N candidate scenes; Top-k is the percentage of queries with the correct scene in the top k. SceneGraphLoc relies on ground-truth scene graphs at inference, whereas CrossWeave needs only a single image and a raw point cloud. CrossWeave still matches it at Top-1 with 10 candidates and exceeds it at Top-5 and Top-10 for both pool sizes, trailing only at Top-1 with 50 candidates. Method 10 candidates 50 candidates Top-1Top-5Top-10 Top-1Top-5Top-10 SceneGraphLoc 53.6081.9092.80 30.2050.2061.20 CrossOver 46.0077.9790.58 18.6939.1651.62 CrossWeave (Ours) 53.6093.10100.0 27.5060.2076.50 Robustness to Noisy Instance Masks We replace ground-truth instance masks with imperfect ones. 2D masks come from MobileSAM prompted with a single click inside the object, keeping the prediction with the highest IoU to the ground truth. 3D masks are corrupted with boundary bleed into neighboring background or objects and contiguous chunk dropout, at a similar IoU degradation. Under combined 2D+3D noise, Top-1 drops by about 6.5 points on ScanNet and 12.2 points on 3RScan, with most of the loss at the stricter R@75% threshold. text_excerpt: OctWorld Long-range generative world modeling OctWorld: Long-Range World-Consistent Video Generation with Octree-based 3D Mapping Zelong Lv1,2,* Sicheng Xu2 Jianfeng Xiang2,3,* Ruicheng Wang1,2,* Yue Dong2 Yu Deng2 Guangzhong Sun1 Jiaolong Yang2,† 1 University of Science and Technology of China 2 Microsoft Research Asia 3 Tsinghua University Read Research Paper Code 01 / Visual overview See OctWorld in motion. OctWorld system workflow OctMap-Guided Generation with Precise Camera Control A system-level visualization of the OctWorld generation workflow, showing how data and conditioning signals flow among camera control, RGB-D generation, OctMap memory, and video diffusion components to enable precise control along user-specified camera trajectories. OctMap online integration Inside OctMap Online Integration A detailed visualization of the OctMap subsystem, showing how incoming RGB-D observations are unprojected, fused into adaptive octree nodes, and integrated online to update the scene's geometry and appearance throughout generation. 02 / Gallery Generated journeys, mapped as they unfold. Hover to play 01 DL3DV trajectories Click Show 3D Map to view the spatial reconstruction. 2 scenes 02 Customized trajectories / DL3DV images Click Show 3D Map to view the spatial reconstruction. 2 scenes 03 Customized trajectories / Synthetic images Click Show 3D Map to view the spatial reconstruction. 14 scenes 03 / Abstract Explorable worlds with persistent 3D memory. We present OctWorld, a video diffusion framework with 3D memory for generating explorable, world-consistent, and high-fidelity visual scenes. Given a single image, OctWorld enables stable autoregressive world generation along user-specified camera trajectories. We focus on the problem of long spatial range generation, characterized by long camera path and wide viewing angle coverage, where maintaining spatial consistency, particularly when revisiting previously generated regions, becomes challenging. To address this, we first build upon a pretrained autoregressive video diffusion model that supports longer-horizon context modeling. We adapt this model to RGB-D generation and introduce a depth normalization scheme for inter-chunk consistency. Next, and more importantly, we propose an extensible and spatially-adaptive 3D memory, termed OctMap. OctMap constructs a global 3D representation of the generated scene by progressively fusing the generated RGB-D frames. To accommodate diverse scene scales in the open world setting, it applies adaptive spatial resolution dynamically determined by image evidence with a sparse octree hierarchy, which preserves effective geometric and appearance details while maintaining low memory overhead. Experiments demonstrate that OctWorld can generate long-range and spatially consistent videos, outperforming prior methods on existing benchmarks as well as in longer-range generation cases. 04 / Method A persistent map for worlds that keep unfolding. Training pipeline of OctWorld. Given a training RGB-D segment, we split the sequence into history frames and target frames. An OctMap is constructed from the history frames and rendered to the target view as spatial conditions. εα and εt denotes gaussian noises at level α and t respectively. 05 / Citation Reference OctWorld. @inproceedings{lv2026octworld, title = {OctWorld: Long-Range World-Consistent Video Generation with Octree-based 3D Mapping}, author = {Lv, Zelong and Xu, Sicheng and Xiang, Jianfeng and Wang, Ruicheng and Dong, Yue and Deng, Yu and Sun, Guangzhong and Yang, Jiaolong}, year = {2026} } Media unavailable

Setup Follow the installation and dataset setup guide. Training and evaluation After preparing the environment and datasets, train and evaluate with: # Train on MegaDepth. bash scripts/reproduce_train/outdoor.sh # Evaluate on MegaDepth-1500, ScanNet-1500, or HPatches. bash scripts/reproduce_test/outdoor.sh megadepth bash scripts/reproduce_test/outdoor.sh scannet bash scripts/reproduce_test/outdoor.sh hpatches Training uses batch size 8 and 20 epochs, saving checkpoints under logs/. Logging uses TensorBoard by default; add --logger wandb to use W&B. Other options are listed by python train.py --help and python test.py --help. Checkpoints Download the pretrained checkpoint from GitHub Releases: mkdir -p weights wget -O weights/outdoor.ckpt \ "https://github.com/mmaiLab/WovenAnchorMatcher/releases/download/v1.0/outdoor.ckpt" Evaluation uses weights/outdoor.ckpt by default; add --ckpt_path /path/to/model.ckpt to use another checkpoint. When no model checkpoint is provided, backbone initialization is downloaded automatically from the JamMa release. Ablations Pass a configuration from configs/woven_anchor/ablations/ to both training and evaluation: bash scripts/reproduce_train/outdoor.sh \ --exp_name inter_crossbimamba \ --ablation_cfg configs/woven_anchor/ablations/inter_crossbimamba.py bash scripts/reproduce_test/outdoor.sh megadepth \ --ablation_cfg configs/woven_anchor/ablations/inter_crossbimamba.py \ --ckpt_path /path/to/inter_crossbimamba.ckpt Visualization and statistics Select a visualization with --vis: Mode Description Output directory qualitative Matches visualization/qualitative/ anchor Assignment maps visualization/anchor_probs/ woven Effective receptive fields visualization/woven_erf/ --vis_max_pairs defaults to 10; use -1 for all pairs or 0 to disable visualization. This limits figures only; evaluation still processes all pairs. bash scripts/reproduce_test/outdoor.sh megadepth --vis anchor --vis_max_pairs 5 bash scripts/reproduce_test/outdoor.sh megadepth --stats_anchor Anchor statistics are aggregated over all evaluation pairs and printed to the log. --vis woven saves PNG figures and raw, unnormalized ERF maps in NPZ files. Measure latency in a separate run without visualization. For single-scene MegaDepth visualization (300 pairs per scene): python test.py configs/data/megadepth_test_0015.py configs/woven_anchor/outdoor/eval.py \ --ckpt_path /path/to/model.ckpt --vis anchor --vis_name 0015 --vis_max_pairs 10 Use configs/data/megadepth_test_0022.py with --vis_name 0022 for scene 0022.
